messages:
matt: Quick follow-up from today's kernel-selection RFC thread — we still need to decide ownership and the runtime surface for choosing between Triton vs CUDA/CUTLASS attention kernels. Two separate concerns: (1) decision logic (heuristics/telemetry) and (2) public fallback/compatibility surface exposed to users.

priya: +1. My main worry is debugging complexity if we hide too much behind an auto-selector. We should provide an opt-out knob and clear logs for why a kernel choice was made. :mag:

jun: Proposal sketch: make kernel selection pluggable and policy-driven. Runtime exposes a small interface (purely in C++/Rust layer) and we supply default policies: "perf-first", "compat-first", "cost-aware". Teams can drop in a new policy. Example API: \n```\ninterface KernelPolicy {\n  string choose(const ModelMeta& m, int seq_len, DType dt, HWProfile hw);\n}\n// runtime calls policy->choose() before enqueueing kernel\n```\nThat keeps selection logic out of serving core and testable.

oliver: How about binary size / dependency surface — if we ship Triton + CUTLASS we risk bloating images and complicating deploys. Can we lazy-load backend libs or mount them as separate sidecars?

marta: Also need to consider attention variant mismatch. Flash attention implementations differ in prefix KV layout and quantization support. If we switch backends mid-request we must ensure KV cache binary compatibility or implement transparent conversion. That's non-trivial.

bench-bot: quick-bench: small warmup perf (toy transformer, 8-layer, 2k seq, fp16) \n```\n- Triton flash-attn: 40 token/sec (stable)\n- CUTLASS custom GEMM+kernel: 36 token/sec (lower mem spikes)\n- Fallback CUDA kernel: 12 token/sec\n```\nNotes: Triton shines at long seq; CUTLASS better memory footprint on 80GB A100.

priya: Given that, I think runtime should prefer Triton for long sequences and CUTLASS for quantized/8-bit workloads where we have tuned ops. But the public surface needs to declare compatibility guarantees (e.g., KV layout, dtype support).

matt: Agreed. Suggested surface: runtime config block (user-editable) + per-request override header. Config example: \n```\nkernel_selection: \n  policy: perf-first\n  allowed_backends: [triton, cutlass, cuda_fallback]\n  override_header: X-Redwood-Kernel\n```\nRuntime logs: "chosen_kernel=triton reason=seq_len>1024 dtype=fp16 hw=A100"

jun: Actionability: split into 3 deliverables with owners + dates: (A) interface + shim (owner: jun) (B) compatibility spec (KV/dtype/layout) (owner: marta) (C) benchmark harness + CI (owner: oliver). Can we add (D) deployment packaging plan (owner: matt/priya)?

marta: I'll draft compatibility spec focusing on: KV layout versioning, tag in model metadata, conversion cost for mid-request conversions, and required tests. ETA 2 weeks.

oliver: I'll wire up a perf harness that runs against A100/RTX8000 and records lat distribution, p99 lat for varying seq_len and batch sizes. Will also test lazy-loading dynamic libs. ETA 10 days.

jun: I'll prototype the KernelPolicy API and a minimal Triton and CUTLASS adapter. Prototype will be minimal (no conversion) to validate hooks. ETA 1 week.

matt: Packaging: we'll try sidecar option first, fallback to multi-stage image if sidecar proves slow. I'll coordinate with eng-infra on CI images. ETA 2 weeks.

bench-bot: Created perf job 1765501250, will post results back here.

priya: One more operational rule: default policy must be conservative for critical tenants (dedicated/private clouds). We should allow org-level default overrides.

matt: Good point — add policy precedence: per-request > org > global. Put that in the interface doc.

priya: Also let's add an observable: "kernel_switch_count" per model to catch thrashing.

jun: +1, will emit metrics and trace reasons.

marta: ACTION ITEMS SUMMARY: \n- jun: implement KernelPolicy shim + basic adapters (1w)\n- marta: compatibility spec draft (2w)\n- oliver: perf harness + lazy-load experiment (10d)\n- matt/priya: deployment/packaging plan + org overrides (2w)\n- bench-bot: run benchmark job and attach full logs (in progress)

matt: Ok let's sync next Tue 10am to review prototypes. If anyone can't make it ping me. Thanks all. :rocket:

oliver: acked. :+1:

priya: Thanks — I'll add the policy precedence and "kernel_switch_count" metric to the RFC as a follow-up.
